chunks.t:
PULSE measures whether your product data can answer what shoppers ask, ranks the repairs worth making, and proves the fix worked. Start with one export.

Most tools here rank what a shopper sees. PULSE asks the question underneath that one: can your
catalogue answer what they came to find out at all? You send a category export, get back the
attributes worth recording in priority order, and re-measure once your team has filled them in.

Nothing goes on your site to begin with. The first useful answer comes from a file.

Who builds this. 
 PULSE is made by Resolve Labs , a small team working on one question: which product
 information is worth paying to fix. The marketing site is
 thepulseapi.com. This site is for the people who have to wire it
 up.

chunks.h: What problem does this actually solve?
chunks.t:
A shopper leaves without buying. Either they could not find the product, or your catalogue could
not tell them apart.

The second one is larger and almost nobody measures it. On a 216-product laptop shelf we
measured, 94 products remain indistinguishable after every question a shopper could answer,
because the attributes that would separate them are not recorded anywhere. No ranking model fixes
that. Only recording the attribute does.

So PULSE starts at the catalogue rather than at the session:

 The question What PULSE answers with 
 --- --- 
 Which missing field costs the most? A ranking by how many shoppers need it, not by how empty the column is 
 Where does that fact already live? Often in your own titles and descriptions, recoverable before anyone types anything 
 Did the repair work? The same measurement on the repaired export, with no traffic needed

}

Six steps, in the order you will meet them. Each one is useful on its own, and you can stop
after any of them.

Or drop it on the page, which is what the storefront integrations use:

 html title="index.html"
<script src="https://cdn.thepulseapi.com/sdk/v0/pulse.iife.js" async </script 
 

The script tag exposes the client as the global Pulse , so Pulse.init(...) works directly.

What leaves the browser. 
 Signals and a session id. Not names, not emails, not payment data. The audit never sees a
 shopper at all: it reads product data.

chunks.h: What should I know before trusting the numbers?

chunks.t:
Every row below is reachable with a publishable key and the x-api-key header. Nothing here
needs a login.

 Endpoint What it is for Counts toward usage SDK method 
 --- --- --- --- 
 POST /track Signals in, personas out Yes track() 
 POST /track/behavior One named behaviour Yes none 
 POST /track/keywords A raw search query, extracted for you Yes none 
 POST /session The personas inferred so far Yes getSession() 
 POST /catalog/ranked Rank the catalogue PULSE holds Yes rankedCatalog() 
 POST /search Rank products you pass in Yes search() 
 POST /rerank Reorder a result set from your own engine Yes none 
 POST /suggest Query suggestions, scored on the session No none 
 POST /catalog/audit What a catalogue cannot answer Yes none 
 POST /catalog/verify What a repair actually changed Yes none 
 POST /event A named outcome No event() 
 POST /exposure What was actually rendered No exposure()

chunks.h: Why three of them are free
chunks.t:
/event and /exposure are how you prove the ranking worked. Charging for measurement makes
switching it off the rational move, which blinds the learning loop and destroys the value case
in the same stroke.

 /suggest fires on every keystroke. Metering it like /search would bill per character typed,
so someone spelling out a query would pay ten times for one search.

Usage is grouped by the first path segment. 
 /track and /track/behavior are both billed as track , and /catalog/ranked ,
 /catalog/audit and /catalog/verify are all billed as catalog . Your invoice shows a line
 per operation rather than one total, because /search costs real compute and /session 
 costs almost nothing.

chunks.h: The four products, and the calls behind them
What is not on this page
chunks.t:
There is a second, much larger API behind a JWT , not an API key: organizations, users,
roles, API keys, catalogue management, billing and subscriptions. That is the management plane
the merchant portal is built on. It is not metered, it is not
sold as a product, and it is not documented here yet.

Treat anything undocumented as unsupported. 
 Routes exist that are not on this page. Some are internal, some are reachable only with a
 login, and some resolve at the gateway and are not served downstream. If it is not written
 down here, do not build on it.
One header, one base URL, and which credential opens what.

Authenticate with x-api-key . Not Authorization: Bearer .

 bash title="A real request"
curl -X POST "https://api.thepulseapi.com/api/v1/session" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -H "x-api-key: pk live ..." \
 -d '{}'

Sign in to the dashboard, open Integration → API keys , and
create one.

 
 --- --- 
 Format Always pk live followed by base64url randomness 
 Publishable Designed to be visible in browser code. It can send signals and read rankings, nothing else 
 Scoped Belongs to one organization and cannot read another's data 
 Shown once The full value is returned only at creation. Only the hash is stored 
 Revocable Revocation is immediate 

There is no test key. 
 Every issued key is pk live . There is no pk test and no sandbox environment yet. To keep
 experiments out of your reporting, create a separate key for development and revoke it when
 you are done.

chunks.h: What a publishable key cannot do
chunks.t:
Catalogue writes ( /products , /categories ) authenticate as a signed-in dashboard session, not
with a publishable key. They are not part of this reference.

POST /catalog/audit and /catalog/verify, which grade catalogue data rather than rank it.

The ranking endpoints answer "which products first". These two answer a different question:
 can this catalogue answer the questions shoppers are asking of it at all. 

Both take a CSV as a string in the body rather than a file upload. An audit is a pure function
over text, so multipart would add a parser, a temporary file and a cleanup path for no gain at a
size where a category export is tens of kilobytes.

Neither call stores anything unless you ask it to.

bash
curl -X POST "https://api.thepulseapi.com/api/v1/catalog/audit" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -H "x-api-key: pk live ..." \
 -d '{
 "csv": "id,category,size,material\n1,helmet,L,abs\n2,helmet,,\n",
 "source": "merchant",
 "amortisationHorizon": 5000
 }'
 

 

Why the horizon is not guessed for you. 
 Without it the response carries no action . Comparing "ask the shopper" against "record the
 fact once" needs to know how many shoppers the fact would serve, and picking a number on your
 behalf would bury the assumption the whole comparison rests on.

The same request does two jobs. Send before and after on their own and it is a monitor: what
changed between two exports, with nothing claimed. Add repairs and the same diff grades the
claims.

 bash
curl -X POST "https://api.thepulseapi.com/api/v1/catalog/verify" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -H "x-api-key: pk live ..." \
 -d '{
 "before": "id,category,size\n1,helmet,\n",
 "after": "id,category,size\n1,helmet,L\n",
 "repairs": [{ "attribute": "size", "method": "manual", "actualHours": 3 }],
 "category": "Helmets"
 }'
 

 

There is no second endpoint for monitoring. 
 Monitor and verification are the same computation over the same diff. The only difference is
 whether anything was claimed about it.

The real response shape, and what each code means.

Every error has the same envelope.

 json title="401 Unauthorized"
{
 "success": false,
 "error": {
 "code": "UNAUTHORIZED",
 "message": "Invalid or revoked API key"
 },
 "timestamp": "2026-10-19T08:27:01.722Z",
 "path": "/api/v1/session",
 "correlationId": "a4cc87c6bf160f30"
}
 

correlationId is the useful field. 
 Quote it when you report a problem. It is how a single request is found in the logs, and it
 turns "ranking looked wrong yesterday" into one lookup.

Code HTTP What it usually means 
 --- --- --- 
 BAD REQUEST 400 Malformed body, or an empty body with a JSON content type 
 UNAUTHORIZED 401 Missing, wrong, or revoked key. Check the header is x-api-key 
 FORBIDDEN 403 The key is valid but not for this organization's data 
 NOT FOUND 404 No such route. Check the /api/v1 prefix 
 TOO MANY REQUESTS 429 Rate limited at the gateway 
 SERVICE UNAVAILABLE 503 A downstream service is failing fast behind its circuit breaker

chunks.h: Two that are worth knowing apart
chunks.t:
401 on every request, including ones that worked yesterday. 
A revoked or expired key returns 401 exactly like a typo. Keys can be given an expiry at
creation. Check the dashboard before debugging your code.
 

404 on a path that exists in the docs. 
The base URL includes the version: https://api.thepulseapi.com/api/v1 . A request to
 thepulseapi.com/v1/... reaches the marketing site, not the API, and will not look like an
API error at all.

POST /exposure, which is what makes ranking quality measurable.

Ranking cannot be graded without knowing what was actually shown. A click rate over results
nobody saw is not a measurement.

ts
pulse.exposure(decisionId, items); // buffered
await pulse.flushExposures(); // send now
 

 exposure buffers, because a product grid renders many items at once and one request per card
would be absurd. flushExposures sends what is pending, and the SDK also flushes on page hide.

Send what rendered, not what you requested. 
 If you asked for 24 and showed 12 above the fold, the honest exposure is what the shopper could
 actually see. Over-reporting exposure makes your own ranking look worse than it is.
/catalog/ranked, /search, /rerank and /suggest.

Ranks the catalogue already synced to PULSE.

 bash
curl -X POST "https://api.thepulseapi.com/api/v1/catalog/ranked" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -H "x-api-key: pk live ..." \
 -d '{
 "sessionId": "sess abc123",
 "organizationId": "org abc123",
 "limit": 24
 }'
 

 ts
const { items } = await pulse.rankedCatalog({ limit: 24 });

Ranks products you pass in , against the session.

 ts
const { results } = await pulse.search(products, { limit: 24 });

results[0].scoreBreakdown; // the signals that matched, and their weights

Reorders an existing result set you already produced elsewhere, which is the lightest way to put
PULSE in front of a search engine you are keeping.

Query suggestions scored against the current session.

 
 search and rankedCatalog are not interchangeable. One ranks what you hand it, the other
 ranks what PULSE holds. Sending a catalogue you already synced to search is a wasted payload.
POST /session, which returns the personas inferred so far.

bash
curl -X POST "https://api.thepulseapi.com/api/v1/session" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -H "x-api-key: pk live ..." \
 -d '{ "sessionId": "sess abc123" }'
 

 ts
const session = await pulse.getSession();
 

Returns whether the session was found and the personas accumulated against it. A session id that
has never been written returns found: false , which is the quickest way to confirm your signals
are landing.

Use this while integrating. 
 If found is false after a track call, the signals are not arriving. That is one request to
 check, rather than reasoning backwards from a ranking that looks slightly wrong.
POST /track, the call everything else depends on.

bash
curl -X POST "https://api.thepulseapi.com/api/v1/track" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -H "x-api-key: pk live ..." \
 -d '{
 "sessionId": "sess abc123",
 "organizationId": "org abc123",
 "signals": [
 { "type": "category view", "value": "helmets-safety" },
 { "type": "price filter", "value": "500000-1500000" }
 ]
 }'
 

With the SDK:

 ts
await pulse.track([
 { type: 'category view', value: 'helmets-safety' },
 { type: 'price filter', value: '500000-1500000' },
]);
 

 
 Signals are additive. Send them as they happen rather than batching a whole session at the end:
 persona scores decay, so ordering carries meaning.
 

organizationId is required. 
 Every endpoint below reads it from the body, not from the API key. Omitting it returns 400 
 with a validation error naming the field. The SDK sends it for you from init() .
 

 /track also captures device, referrer and time from the request itself, so a call with no
 signals at all is still worth making: it opens the session with what the request already says.

One behaviour, named, when you have nothing to say about a category or a price.

 bash
curl -X POST "https://api.thepulseapi.com/api/v1/track/behavior" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -H "x-api-key: pk live ..." \
 -d '{
 "sessionId": "sess abc123",
 "organizationId": "org abc123",
 "behavior": "sort price asc",
 "metadata": { "page": "category" }
 }'
 

 behavior is your own slug, capped at 128 characters. Sorting by price ascending says something
about a shopper that no category view does.

A search query, turned into keyword signals for you.

 bash
curl -X POST "https://api.thepulseapi.com/api/v1/track/keywords" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -H "x-api-key: pk live ..." \
 -d '{
 "sessionId": "sess abc123",
 "organizationId": "org abc123",
 "query": "mu bao hiem fullface"
 }'
 

Send the raw query. Extraction happens server-side, and the query is capped at 512 characters
because the work is linear in its length.
What is versioned, what is not, and what happens when something changes.

chunks.h: The API is versioned. The guides are not.
chunks.t:
Versioned Why 
 --- --- --- 
 API reference Yes , /api/v1 It is a contract. A request you wrote last year has to keep working, so the page describing it has to keep existing 
 Guides, concepts, frameworks No They describe behaviour, not a contract. "How inference works" has no v1 and v2 
 SDK reference No The SDK follows the API. Where a method needs a minimum version, the page says so inline 

The version in the docs URL matches the version in the request URL:

 bash
https://api.thepulseapi.com/api/v1/track → /api/v1/track
 

Only v1 exists. 
 There has never been another. The path carries the version anyway, because a URL is cheap to
 choose now and expensive to change once people have linked to it.

chunks.h: What counts as a breaking change
chunks.t:
A new major version happens only when an existing, correct request would start behaving
differently.

 
Breaking: needs a new version. 
- Removing an endpoint, a field, or an accepted value
- Renaming anything in a request or response
- Making an optional request field required
- Narrowing a type, for example a string that becomes an enum
- Changing the meaning of a field while keeping its name. This is the worst one , because nothing fails loudly
 

Not breaking: ships into the current version. 
- Adding a new endpoint
- Adding an optional request field
- Adding a field to a response. Parse responses permissively : unknown fields will appear
- Adding a new value to an output enum, unless the docs say the set is closed
- Making a validation message clearer

chunks.h: What we owe you when a version changes
chunks.t:
1. A new path, /api/v1/v2 , with v1 still published and still working 
2. A migration page naming every behavioural difference, not a summary
3. A deprecation notice on each v1 page pointing at its v2 equivalent
4. A stated end date for v1, not "eventually"

@thepulseapi/sdk follows
semver and tracks the API rather than mirroring it.

While the SDK is 0.x. 
 Pre-1.0, a minor version may contain a breaking change. That is what 0.x means in semver,
 and it is worth pinning an exact version until 1.0.
 

The CDN build is versioned the same way, with an immutable path per release and a floating major:

 
https://cdn.thepulseapi.com/sdk/v0.1.5/pulse.iife.js exact, never changes
https://cdn.thepulseapi.com/sdk/v0/pulse.iife.js patches arrive here

PULSE from a server, in any language that can send JSON over HTTPS.

There is no PULSE library for your backend language, and you do not need one. Every endpoint is
 POST , every body is JSON, and authentication is one header.

 
POST https://api.thepulseapi.com/api/v1/<endpoint 
Content-Type: application/json
x-api-key: pk live ...
 

That is the whole integration surface. The guides in this section are the same three calls
written idiomatically per language, so you can copy one and delete the rest.

chunks.h: Which calls belong on a server
One thing to get right first
chunks.t:
sessionId and organizationId are required on nearly every call, and both come from the body
rather than from the API key. A request without them returns 400 with the field named. See
Send signals.

A session is yours to name. It is a string you generate, up to 128 characters, and the only rule
is that the same shopper keeps the same one. If the browser is already running the SDK, read it
with pulse.getSessionId() and pass it to your server rather than inventing a second session for
the same person.

There is one kind of key. 
 Keys are pk live , publishable, and the same key works from a browser and from a server.
 There is no separate secret key today, which means a key leaked from your server is no worse
 and no better than one read out of your page source. Scope and rotate accordingly.

A typed HttpClient, registered once, injected where it is needed.

No package to install. HttpClient and System.Text.Json are in the framework.

Property names. 
 System.Text.Json serialises anonymous object members verbatim, so sessionId stays
 sessionId . If you swap in a named class with PascalCase properties, set
 JsonNamingPolicy.CamelCase or the API will reject the body as missing its required fields.

Two timeouts, not one. 
 connectTimeout on the client and timeout on the request do different jobs. Set only the
 first and a server that accepts your connection and then stalls will hold the thread
 indefinitely.

cURL from the standard library, and Guzzle where a framework already ships it.

For the browser half of a PHP app, see the Laravel guide. This page is the
server half: calls your PHP makes itself.

requests or httpx, plus where the call belongs in Django and FastAPI.

Or requests , if it is already in the project. Both work; httpx is here because it gives you
the async client FastAPI wants without a second dependency.

Build the client once at module level, not per request. httpx.Client keeps a connection pool
and creating one per view throws that away.

 python title="catalog/views.py"
from django.shortcuts import render
from .pulse import pulse

def category(request, slug):
 # The browser owns the session. Read it rather than minting a second one for the
 # same shopper: two session ids means the inference starts from nothing twice.
 session id = request.COOKIES.get("pulse session")
 products = []

 if session id:
 try:
 products = pulse.ranked catalog(session id, limit=24, categorySlug=slug)["items"]
 except Exception:
 # Ranking is an enhancement. A page that fails to render because personalisation
 # was slow is worse than a page in catalogue order.
 products = []

 return render(request, "category.html", {"products": products or default order(slug)})

Use the async client, and hold it on the app so it is created once and closed on shutdown.

 python title="main.py"

from contextlib import asynccontextmanager

from fastapi import FastAPI

BASE = "https://api.thepulseapi.com/api/v1"
ORG = os.environ["PULSE ORG ID"]

@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
 app.state.pulse = httpx.AsyncClient(
 base url=BASE,
 timeout=5.0,
 headers={"x-api-key": os.environ["PULSE API KEY"]},
 )
 yield
 await app.state.pulse.aclose()

app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)

@app.get("/ranked/{session id}")
async def ranked(session id: str, limit: int = 24):
 response = await app.state.pulse.post(
 "/catalog/ranked",
 json={"sessionId": session id, "organizationId": ORG, "limit": limit},
 )
 response.raise for status()
 return response.json()
 

Give it a timeout. 
 Neither requests nor httpx has a default timeout in the shape most people expect. A
 ranking call that hangs will hold a worker until something else gives up. Five seconds is
 generous; the call is usually tens of milliseconds.

net/http from the standard library. Nothing to add to the Gemfile.

ruby title="lib/pulse.rb"
require "json"
require "net/http"
require "uri"

class Pulse
 BASE = URI("https://api.thepulseapi.com/api/v1").freeze

 def initialize(api key:, organization id:)
 @api key = api key
 @organization id = organization id
 end

 def track(session id, signals)
 post("/track", sessionId: session id, signals: signals)
 end

 def ranked catalog(session id, limit: 24)
 post("/catalog/ranked", sessionId: session id, limit: limit)
 end

 def session(session id)
 post("/session", sessionId: session id)
 end

 private

 def post(path, body)
 # organizationId is required on nearly every endpoint and is read from the body,
 # not from the key.
 body[:organizationId] = @organization id

 request = Net::HTTP::Post.new(BASE.path + path)
 request["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
 request["x-api-key"] = @api key
 request.body = JSON.generate(body)

 response = Net::HTTP.start(
 BASE.host, BASE.port,
 use ssl: true,
 open timeout: 5,
 read timeout: 5,
 ) { http http.request(request) }

 raise "PULSE #{path}: #{response.code}" unless response.is a?(Net::HTTPSuccess)

 JSON.parse(response.body)
 end
end

ruby title="config/initializers/pulse.rb"
PULSE = Pulse.new(
 api key: ENV.fetch("PULSE API KEY"),
 organization id: ENV.fetch("PULSE ORG ID"),
)
 

 ruby title="app/controllers/catalog controller.rb"
def show
 session id = cookies[:pulse session]
 @products = if session id
 PULSE.ranked catalog(session id, limit: 24)["items"]
 end
rescue StandardError
 # Personalisation is an enhancement. Catalogue order is a working page.
 @products = nil
ensure
 @products = Product.where(category: params[:slug]).limit(24)
end
 

Both timeouts. 
 open timeout bounds the connection and read timeout bounds the wait for a response. Set
 only the first and a server that accepts your connection and then stalls holds the request
 until something upstream gives up.

set sensitive on the key header. 
 It keeps the value out of Debug output for the header map, which is the kind of log line
 that ends up in an error report without anyone deciding to put it there.

Every change to these pages, newest first, read from git at build time rather than written by hand.

What changed on this site, and when. The list is read from the repository's own history when the
site is built, so it cannot drift from what actually happened and nobody has to remember to
update it.

This is not the API changelog. 
 The API's compatibility rules, what counts as a breaking change and what we owe you when one
 happens, are on Versioning. The API is versioned by URL and these guides
 are not , which is a deliberate choice explained there. This page is the history of the
 documentation itself.

Every page carries the date it last changed at the foot of the page, beside a link to that one
file's full commit history. That is the quickest way to answer "did this page say something
different last month", which is usually the real question.

The pages are MDX files in
 content/docs , so the history is
ordinary git: every revision, who made it, and what else changed in the same commit.

The persona updates. Each signal moves a set of persona scores. Scores decay, so a session that changes direction
is followed rather than averaged.

Products are scored against it. search ranks products you pass in. rankedCatalog ranks the catalogue already synced to PULSE.

Exposure is recorded. What was actually shown is what makes ranking quality measurable later. See
 exposure .

Each signal moves a set of persona scores. Scores decay, so a session that changes direction
is followed rather than averaged.
search ranks products you pass in. rankedCatalog ranks the catalogue already synced to PULSE.

What was actually shown is what makes ranking quality measurable later. See

PULSE is not a PIM and it replaces nothing you already run. It reads your catalogue and ranks

How long a session lives, what identifies it, and how to reset one.

A session is the unit everything attaches to. It is created by init() and held in browser
storage.

 ts
pulse.getSessionId(); // 'sess ...'
pulse.resetSession(); // start clean
await pulse.getSession(); // current personas, server side

Default 
 --- --- --- 
 sessionTtlMs 30 minutes Inactivity before a new session starts

What you send, what is captured for you, and what is deliberately not a signal.

A signal is one observation about the current session. Send them with
 track .

 ts
await pulse.track([
 { type: 'category view', value: 'helmets-safety' },
 { type: 'product view', value: 'sku-123' },
 { type: 'price filter', value: '500000-1500000' },
]);

init() sends these once per session, unless autoTrack: false :

 
 --- --- 
 Device Class and capability, parsed from the user agent 
 Referrer Where the session came from 
 Time of day Local hour bucket 

They cost no network beyond the one call, and they are exported individually so a host app can
re-assert them on a later page load:

 ts

anonymousId never reaches inference. 
 anonymousId is an identity label. Nothing in the engine matches on it, so labelling a session
 cannot change what is inferred about it. That separation is deliberate: it makes it possible to
 attribute a session without contaminating the result.
 

Age, gender, job title and income are not inputs. The engine reads behaviour. If you hold
those attributes, they are ground truth to grade against, not features to feed in.

Why the emptiest column is usually the wrong one to fix, what a bit of decision information buys, and the three cases where the ranking is wrong.

The audit returns attributes in priority order. The order is the product, and it is not the order
you would get by counting blanks.

chunks.h: Why not just fix the emptiest column?
chunks.t:
Because emptiness and usefulness are different quantities, and on a real shelf they invert.

Here are two attributes from the 216-product laptop catalogue we use for our own research:

 Attribute Missing on Rank by emptiness Rank by decision value 
 --- --- --- --- 
 Processor 162 of 216 1st last 
 Screen size 80 of 216 4th 1st 

Processor is missing twice as often and almost nobody is deciding on it: it appears in 2 of the 32
buying requirements we tested. Screen size appears in 13. Fill processor everywhere and you have
done the most visible work on the dashboard and moved the fewest decisions.

This is the whole argument. 
 A completeness score measures your catalogue against itself. The audit measures it against what
 shoppers are trying to decide. Those produce different work orders, and only one of them is
 ranked by what it buys.

chunks.h: What is a bit of decision information?
chunks.t:
One bit is one halving of the shelf.

If a shopper faces 216 products and an attribute splits them cleanly in two, that attribute is
worth one bit: it takes 216 to 108. Two bits takes it to 54. The audit reports what each attribute
would be worth if it were recorded everywhere , minus what it is worth today, and the
difference is what the repair buys.

This is why the number is not a percentage. A percentage tells you how full a column is. Bits tell
you how much closer a shopper gets to a decision when you fill it.

chunks.h: Where does the missing value already live?
chunks.t:
Often in text you already own. Before recommending that anyone type anything, the audit tries to
recover the value from your own titles and descriptions.

On that same laptop shelf, 161 of 216 missing screen sizes were already sitting in the product
titles . That is a parse, not a procurement project, and it changes what the repair costs enough
to change whether it is worth doing.

The audit reports each attribute's provenance so you can tell the two apart:

 Where the fact is What the repair actually is 
 --- --- 
 Already in your text Extraction. Cheap, and often same-day 
 In a supplier feed Mapping. A ticket, not a project 
 Nowhere Acquisition. Someone has to go and find it

Three cases, and we would rather you heard them from us.

The recorded values are not representative. Simulating a complete catalogue can only draw on values your shelf already holds. If an attribute
is recorded on twenty products and those twenty are not typical of the range, the simulation is
wrong in a way we can name and cannot yet correct.

The requirements are not yours. The buying requirements we test against are typed from public category guides and filter rails. If
your shoppers want something those do not cover, the ranking will not know. Sending us your own
search and filter logs is what fixes this, and it is the single highest-value thing you can add.

The fact exists only in a photograph. A dietary claim printed on a pack, a material visible in an image. We can tell you the attribute
is missing from your fields. We cannot yet read it out of your imagery, and we will say so on the
row rather than quietly scoring it as absent.

No build step. The global, used straight from HTML attributes.

Alpine is attribute-driven, so the script-tag build is the natural fit. No bundler, no install.

 html title="index.html"
<script src="https://cdn.thepulseapi.com/sdk/v0/pulse.iife.js" </script 
<script 
 Pulse.init({ apiKey: 'pk live ...', organizationId: 'org ...' });
</script 
 

The global Pulse is the client, so call it directly from Alpine:

 html
<div x-data="{ sku: 'sku-123' }" 
 <button x-on:click="Pulse.track([{ type: 'product view', value: sku }])" 
 View
 </button 

 <button x-on:click="Pulse.track([{ type: 'add to cart', value: sku }])" 
 Add to cart
 </button 
</div 
 

 
 There is no default export on the global. Pulse.init resolves; Pulse.default.init does not.

Islands use the React or Vue guide. A plain page is one script tag.

Astro ships whichever island framework you already use, so for islands follow
React or Vue.

For a plain Astro page, this is the whole integration:

 astro title="src/layouts/Base.astro"
<script 

 const pulse = new PulseClient();
 pulse.init({
 apiKey: import.meta.env.PUBLIC PULSE API KEY,
 organizationId: import.meta.env.PUBLIC PULSE ORG ID,
 });
</script 
 

 

Or skip the install entirely and use the CDN build:

 astro
<script is:inline src="https://cdn.thepulseapi.com/sdk/v0/pulse.iife.js" </script

A Blade partial for the browser half. Secrets stay on the server.

Laravel renders on the server, so the browser half is a script tag, usually in a layout.

 php title="config/services.php"
'pulse' = [
 'key' = env('PULSE PUBLISHABLE KEY'),
 'org' = env('PULSE ORGANIZATION ID'),
],
 

 blade title="resources/views/partials/pulse.blade.php"
<script src="https://cdn.thepulseapi.com/sdk/v0/pulse.iife.js" </script 
<script 
 Pulse.init({
 apiKey: @json(config('services.pulse.key')),
 organizationId: @json(config('services.pulse.org')),
 });
</script 
 

 blade title="resources/views/layouts/app.blade.php"
@include('partials.pulse')
 

Which key goes in the page. 
 The publishable pk live key is designed to be visible in browser code. Anything that
 administers your account is not. Use @json() rather than string interpolation so a value
 containing a quote cannot break out of the script.

To talk to PULSE from PHP rather than the browser, use the REST API directly. There
is no PHP package yet.
Create the client once, share it, and keep init() in the browser.

What to check before you ship PULSE, what to watch in the first week, and the claims we will not make for you.

You have run an audit, repaired something, and possibly wired up the runtime. This page is the
end of the path: what to check before it goes in front of shoppers, and what to expect
afterwards.

chunks.h: What should I check before shipping?
chunks.t:
Keys are the right kind. A publishable key ( pk live ... ) is designed to be visible in page source. A secret key is not,
and belongs only in a server guide. If a secret key reached a theme file or a client bundle,
revoke it now rather than after the deploy.

A held-back group exists. Decide what fraction of traffic never sees PULSE ranking, and keep it. Without a control arm you
cannot tell a good quarter from a good ranker, and you will not be able to answer the first
question your finance team asks.

Your own order is the fallback. If the engine is slow or unavailable, the page should render your existing order rather than an
empty shelf. Check it by pointing endpoint at a port nothing is listening on and loading the
page.

`init()` failure is visible to you. init() sends the automatic signals exactly once and swallows its own error. A session whose
 init() failed stays thin for its whole life, and nothing in the page tells you. Log the
failure, or call
 captureAutoSignals() again on a later page load.

chunks.h: What should I check before shipping?
chunks.t:
Exposure is recorded. If you rank, call exposure() with what was actually rendered. A ranking you cannot tie to what
the shopper saw cannot be evaluated later, and the buffered call costs almost nothing.

and belongs only in a server guide. If a secret key reached a theme file or a client bundle,
revoke it now rather than after the deploy.

chunks.h: What should I watch in the first week?
chunks.t:
Watch Why it matters 
 --- --- 
 Sessions with zero signals Almost always init() failing silently, or a key scoped to the wrong origin 
 Abstention rate The engine declining to rank is working as designed. A sudden move in it usually means the catalogue changed, not the engine 
 Audit readiness, re-run Catalogues decay. New products arrive unrecorded, and a shelf that scored well last quarter quietly stops 
 Fallback rate How often your own order was served instead. Should be near zero and is not always

chunks.h: What will you not claim for me?
chunks.t:
Worth reading before you repeat anything from this site internally.

No uplift number. 
 We have run no live revenue experiment. We will not quote a conversion lift, a return-rate
 reduction or an ROI multiple, and any figure you see elsewhere attached to those words did not
 come from us.
 

What we can show is a property of your catalogue: which requirements it can and cannot resolve,
before and after a repair. That is measured, it is reproducible, and it is not the same thing as
a sale.

Three more limits, stated plainly:

- A fact that exists only inside a photograph is one we can tell you is missing and cannot yet
 recover for you. Extracting attributes from product imagery is research we are doing, not a
 feature we ship.
- Our simulation of a complete catalogue can only use values your shelf already records. 
 Where an attribute's recorded values do not represent its true range, the simulation is wrong
 in a way we can name and cannot yet correct.
- We have no customers to name. When that changes we will say so with their permission.

Connect the PULSE documentation to Claude, Cursor or any MCP client, so an agent can search and read every page instead of guessing.

Every page on this site is available to an agent over the Model Context Protocol. An assistant
with this connected searches the documentation and quotes it, instead of recalling an endpoint
that may not exist.

Tool What it does 
 --- --- 
 search docs Full-text search across every page. Returns the matching section, its URL and a score 
 get page One page as Markdown, by path, such as /quickstart or /api/v1/audit 
 list pages Every page with its title, for orienting before a search 

All three take a lang of en or vi .

chunks.h: Why is the search lexical rather than semantic?
chunks.t:
The website embeds your question with a model it has already downloaded. Making an agent download
one to ask a question is a poor trade, because the agent is itself a language model: it can read
three candidate sections and decide which is right far better than a cosine can.

It also matters that an agent asking about /catalog/audit wants the page containing that exact
string, and lexical scoring is precise about that where an embedding blurs it.

chunks.h: What if I want it pointed somewhere else?
chunks.t:
Set PULSE DOCS ORIGIN to serve from a different origin, which is mostly useful when you are
working on the documentation itself:

 bash
PULSE DOCS ORIGIN=http://localhost:3000 npx @thepulseapi/docs-mcp

chunks.h: Can I just read the Markdown?
chunks.t:
Yes, and you do not need MCP for it.

 
 --- --- 
 /llms.txt Every page, titled and linked, in one file 
 /llms-full.txt The whole documentation as one Markdown document 
 /llms.mdx/docs/<path /content.md Any single page as Markdown 
 /search-index.json The chunked corpus with its embeddings 

Each page also carries a Copy Markdown button, which is the fastest route when you just want
to paste one page into a conversation.

What works on a hosted storefront today, and what is still a script tag rather than an app.

There is no PULSE app or plugin yet. 
 Not in the Shopify App Store, not on the WordPress plugin directory, not in the Magento
 Marketplace. Anyone telling you otherwise is describing a plan. What exists today is the
 script tag, and it works on all three.
 

That is less of a limitation than it sounds. PULSE needs three things from a storefront: the
script, an init call with your keys, and signals describing what the shopper is looking at.
Every platform here can supply all three from its own theme templates, which is also the only
place that knows what page the shopper is on.

 
 } title="Shopify" href="/platforms/shopify" description="theme.liquid, with signals from Liquid objects." / 
 } title="WordPress and WooCommerce" href="/platforms/wordpress" description="wp enqueue script, with signals from the WooCommerce conditionals." / 
 } title="Magento 2" href="/platforms/magento" description="Layout XML and a template block." /

Worth being precise about what you give up by pasting a script instead:

 Script tag, today An app or plugin 
 --- --- --- 
 Install Paste into a theme file One click, no theme edit 
 Keys Typed into the theme Entered in an admin screen 
 Survives a theme change No Yes 
 Catalogue sync You send products per request Pushed and kept current 
 Signals You write them per template Mapped for you 

The first four rows are convenience. The fifth is where the difference actually lives, and it is
also why a plugin is not just packaging: a good one knows what a "collection page" means on that
platform and sends the right signal without being told.

Anything that lets you add a script to a page can run the browser SDK, and anything that can
make an HTTPS request can call the API directly. If your platform is not listed, the
Alpine guide is the closest shape: a script tag and HTML attributes, no
build step. For server-side work, see Backend.

Layout XML and a template block, which is how Magento adds a script.

Not on the Marketplace. 
 No PULSE extension exists. This is a small module you add yourself, in the shape Magento
 expects.
 

Magento does not take a pasted script tag. Markup belongs to a template, templates are attached
by layout XML, and both live in a module. That is three files before anything runs, which is the
platform rather than PULSE.

php title="app/code/Pulse/Tracking/registration.php"
<?php
\Magento\Framework\Component\ComponentRegistrar::register(
 \Magento\Framework\Component\ComponentRegistrar::MODULE,
 'Pulse Tracking',
 DIR 
);
 

 xml title="app/code/Pulse/Tracking/etc/module.xml"
<?xml version="1.0"? 
<config xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
 xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:Module/etc/module.xsd" 
 <module name="Pulse Tracking" setup version="1.0.0"/ 
</config

default.xml applies to every page, which is what you want for init .

 xml title="app/code/Pulse/Tracking/view/frontend/layout/default.xml"
<?xml version="1.0"? 
<page xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
 layout="1column"
 xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:View/Layout/etc/page configuration.xsd" 
 <head 
 <script src="https://cdn.thepulseapi.com/sdk/v0/pulse.iife.js" src type="url" async="true"/ 
 </head 
 <body 
 <referenceContainer name="before.body.end" 
 <block class="Magento\Framework\View\Element\Template"
 name="pulse.init"
 template="Pulse Tracking::init.phtml"/ 
 </referenceContainer 
 </body 
</page 
 

 src type="url" is load bearing. Without it Magento treats the path as a local static asset and
tries to resolve it inside pub/static , where it does not exist.

 php title="app/code/Pulse/Tracking/view/frontend/templates/init.phtml"
<script 
 window.addEventListener('load', function () {
 Pulse.init({
 apiKey: <?= $block- escapeJs($block- getPulseApiKey()) ? ,
 organizationId: <?= $block- escapeJs($block- getPulseOrgId()) ? 
 });
 });
</script

Category and product pages each get their own layout handle, so each can attach its own block
without any conditional logic.

 xml title="view/frontend/layout/catalog category view.xml"
<?xml version="1.0"? 
<page xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
 xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="urn:magento:framework:View/Layout/etc/page configuration.xsd" 
 <body 
 <referenceContainer name="before.body.end" 
 <block class="Pulse\Tracking\Block\Category"
 name="pulse.category"
 template="Pulse Tracking::category.phtml"/ 
 </referenceContainer 
 </body 
</page 
 

The equivalent file for products is catalog product view.xml . Each template sends one track 
call built from the registry object its block resolves.

Keys belong in system configuration. 
 Hard-coding them in a template means a deployment to change a key. A system.xml field read
 through ScopeConfigInterface puts them in the admin, which is also where a store operator
 expects to find them.

One script tag in theme.liquid, and signals built from Liquid objects.

Not an App Store app. 
 This is a theme edit. It does not survive switching themes, and it puts your keys in a theme
 file that anyone with theme access can read. Publishable keys are designed to be visible in
 page source, so that is a housekeeping problem rather than a security one.

Checkout. Shopify does not let a theme script run on checkout pages outside Plus, so purchase
outcomes have to come from your server via a webhook, not from the browser. See
Backend for the call to make when the webhook arrives.

wp_enqueue_script in a small plugin, with signals from the WooCommerce conditionals.

Not on the plugin directory. 
 There is no PULSE plugin to install. What follows is a short one you write yourself, which is
 perhaps twenty lines and does not need to be anything more.

chunks.h: Write it as a plugin, not a theme edit
Write it as a plugin, not a theme edit

chunks.t: From nothing to a ranked catalogue in about ten lines.

Sign in to the dashboard and open Integration → API keys .
Create a key, name it for where it will run, and copy it immediately.

Shown once. 
 The full key is returned only at creation. Only its hash is stored. If you lose it, revoke it
 and create another.
 

Your organization id is on the same page. You need both.

ts
const { results } = await pulse.search(products);

results[0].scoreBreakdown; // why this one came first
 

Every result carries the signals that matched it, so you can show a shopper why, or show
yourself why when it looks wrong.

html title="index.html"
<script src="https://cdn.thepulseapi.com/sdk/v0/pulse.iife.js" </script 
<script 
 Pulse.init({ apiKey: 'pk live ...', organizationId: 'org ...' });
</script
Every method on PulseClient, the config it takes, and the functions the package exports beside it.

Method Returns 
 --- --- --- 
 init(config) TrackResponse \ null Start a session and send the automatic signals once 
 getSession() SessionResponse Current session and inferred personas 
 getSessionId() string The current session id 
 resetSession() void Clear it and start fresh 
 onPersona(cb) void Subscribe to persona updates

Method Returns 
 --- --- --- 
 track(signals) TrackResponse Send shopper signals 
 search(products, options?) SearchResponse Rank products you pass in 
 rankedCatalog(options?) RankedCatalogResponse Rank the catalogue already synced to PULSE 
 event(type, data?) EventResponse Record a named event 

 
 search and rankedCatalog are not interchangeable. search ranks what you hand it;
 rankedCatalog ranks what PULSE already holds.

Method 
 --- --- --- 
 exposure(decisionId, items) void Record what was actually rendered, buffered 
 flushExposures() Promise<void Send buffered exposures now

PulseClient is most of the package and not all of it. These are exported too, for the cases
where you need a signal without a client, or need to look at what the SDK cached.

init() calls captureAutoSignals() for you when autoTrack is on, so you only need these
directly when you want a signal at a different moment, or want one the automatic set leaves out.

 Export Returns 
 --- --- --- 
 captureAutoSignals() Signal[] Device, referrer and time in one call. What init() sends 
 captureDeviceSignal() Signal \ null Device class from the user agent 
 captureReferrerSignal() Signal \ null Where the visit came from 
 captureTimeSignal() Signal Time of day. Never null, there is always a clock 
 captureEnhancedReferrerSignals() Signal[] Campaign and channel detail beyond the plain referrer 
 captureDeviceInfoAsync(): Promise DeviceInfo Fuller device detail, including client hints 
 captureGeoInfo(): Promise GeoInfo \ null Coarse location from the IP 
 geoToSignals(geo) Signal[] Turn a GeoInfo into signals 
 captureWeatherInfo(lat, lon, apiKey?): Promise WeatherInfo \ null Conditions at a point 
 weatherToSignals(weather) Signal[] Turn a WeatherInfo into signals 
 captureCulturalCalendar(countryCode) Signal[] Seasonal and cultural events active today 
 parseUserAgent(ua) DeviceInfo Parse a user agent string you already have

captureWeatherInfo needs your own key. 
 It calls OpenWeatherMap and returns null without an apiKey , so nothing breaks if you leave
 it out. The free tier is 1,000 calls a day, which is why the result is cached per session
 rather than fetched per page.
 

 
 captureAutoSignals() is exported for one specific failure. init() sends the automatic
 signals exactly once and swallows its own error, so a session whose init() failed never
 re-sends them and stays thin for its whole life. These signals cost no network of their own, so
 calling this again on a later page load is cheaper than the alternative.

Device, location and weather are properties of the session rather than of the page: they cannot
change between one page and the next. The SDK captures them once, keys the cache by session id so
it cannot outlive the visitor it describes, and reuses it. You rarely need to touch this.

 Export Returns 
 --- --- --- 
 readSessionContext(sessionId) SessionContext \ null The cache, or null if it belongs to another session 
 writeSessionContext(sessionId, patch) void Merge fields into it 
 isWeatherFresh(ctx, now?) boolean Whether the weather reading is still inside its TTL 
 clearSessionContext() void Drop the cache 
 WEATHER TTL MS number 10 minutes 

 
 Weather is the only field here with a TTL. Everything else is immutable for the session, but a
 30-minute session can outlast a rain shower, and a weather:rain signal driving a
 recommendation after the sun came out is the engine being confidently wrong.

PULSE đo xem dữ liệu sản phẩm của bạn có trả lời được điều người mua đang hỏi hay không, xếp hạng những chỗ đáng sửa, và chứng minh bản sửa có tác dụng.

Phần lớn công cụ ở lĩnh vực này xếp hạng những gì người mua nhìn thấy. PULSE hỏi câu nằm bên
dưới câu đó: danh mục của bạn có trả lời được điều họ đến để tìm hiểu hay không? Bạn gửi một tệp
xuất ngành hàng, nhận lại các thuộc tính đáng ghi theo thứ tự ưu tiên, rồi đo lại sau khi đội của
bạn đã điền xong.

Ban đầu không có gì được cài lên website của bạn. Câu trả lời hữu ích đầu tiên đến từ một tệp.

Ai xây dựng sản phẩm này. 
 PULSE do Resolve Labs làm ra, một đội nhỏ theo đuổi một câu hỏi: thông tin sản phẩm nào đáng
 bỏ tiền ra sửa. Trang giới thiệu là thepulseapi.com. Trang này
 dành cho những người phải tích hợp nó.

chunks.h: Sản phẩm này thực sự giải quyết vấn đề gì?
chunks.t:
Một người mua rời đi mà không mua gì. Hoặc là họ không tìm thấy sản phẩm, hoặc là danh mục của bạn
không giúp họ phân biệt được các sản phẩm với nhau.

Vế thứ hai lớn hơn và gần như không ai đo nó. Trên một kệ 216 mẫu laptop mà chúng tôi đã đo,
 94 sản phẩm vẫn không thể phân biệt được sau mọi câu hỏi mà người mua có thể trả lời, bởi vì
những thuộc tính giúp tách chúng ra không được ghi ở đâu cả. Không mô hình xếp hạng nào sửa được
điều đó. Chỉ có việc ghi lại thuộc tính mới sửa được.

Nên PULSE bắt đầu từ danh mục chứ không phải từ phiên truy cập:

 Câu hỏi PULSE trả lời bằng 
 --- --- 
 Trường dữ liệu còn thiếu nào tốn kém nhất? Một bảng xếp hạng theo số người mua cần nó, không phải theo mức độ trống của cột 
 Dữ kiện đó vốn đang nằm ở đâu? Thường là trong chính tiêu đề và mô tả của bạn, lấy lại được trước khi ai đó phải gõ gì 
 Bản sửa có tác dụng không? Cùng một phép đo trên tệp xuất đã sửa, không cần lưu lượng truy cập

}

chunks.h: Toàn bộ hành trình trông ra sao?
chunks.t:
Sáu bước, theo đúng thứ tự bạn sẽ gặp. Mỗi bước tự nó đã hữu ích, và bạn có thể dừng lại sau bất
kỳ bước nào.

Đo danh mục. POST /catalog/audit nhận một tệp xuất ngành hàng và trả về các thuộc tính đáng ghi, đã xếp hạng,
kèm danh sách sản phẩm bị ảnh hưởng. Không lưu trạng thái, và không lưu gì trừ khi bạn yêu cầu.

Chạy bản kiểm tra đầu tiên

Hiểu kết quả trả về. Thứ hạng được đo bằng bit thông tin quyết định, không phải đoán từ lượt nhấp, và cột trống nhất
thường là cột không đáng sửa nhất.

Bản kiểm tra đo gì

Sửa, rồi đo lại. Đội của bạn điền thuộc tính đứng đầu bảng. POST /catalog/verify chạy lại đúng phép đo đó trên
tệp xuất đã sửa và báo cáo điều gì đã thay đổi, theo từng thuộc tính. Nó đọc danh mục chứ không
đọc lưu lượng, nên không phải chờ gì cả.

Tài liệu endpoint

Đưa vào hệ thống của bạn. Chỉ cần khi bạn muốn dùng phần thời gian thực. Có hướng dẫn cho React, Vue, Angular, Astro, Alpine
và Laravel; hướng dẫn gian hàng cho Shopify, WordPress và Magento; hướng dẫn máy chủ cho tám ngôn
ngữ.

Framework · Gian hàng · Máy chủ

chunks.h: Toàn bộ hành trình trông ra sao?
chunks.t:
Xếp hạng phiên truy cập, nếu bạn muốn. Phần tuỳ chọn, và là phần duy nhất chạm tới gian hàng của bạn. SDK gửi tín hiệu, bộ máy xếp hạng
danh mục theo những gì phiên truy cập hàm ý, và mọi điểm số đều kèm diễn giải theo từng yếu tố.

Tài liệu SDK · Tài liệu API

POST /catalog/audit nhận một tệp xuất ngành hàng và trả về các thuộc tính đáng ghi, đã xếp hạng,
kèm danh sách sản phẩm bị ảnh hưởng. Không lưu trạng thái, và không lưu gì trừ khi bạn yêu cầu.

Chạy bản kiểm tra đầu tiên

Thứ hạng được đo bằng bit thông tin quyết định, không phải đoán từ lượt nhấp, và cột trống nhất
thường là cột không đáng sửa nhất.

Tài liệu SDK · Tài liệu API

Cần kiểm tra gì trước khi phát hành, cần theo dõi gì sau đó, và những điều chúng tôi sẽ không
tuyên bố.

Đưa lên production

Hoặc nhúng thẳng vào trang, đây là cách các bản tích hợp gian hàng đang dùng:

 html title="index.html"
<script src="https://cdn.thepulseapi.com/sdk/v0/pulse.iife.js" async </script 
 

Thẻ script này expose client ra biến toàn cục Pulse , nên gọi Pulse.init(...) là chạy được ngay.

Những gì rời khỏi trình duyệt. 
 Tín hiệu và một mã phiên. Không có tên, không có email, không có dữ liệu thanh toán. Bản kiểm
 tra thì không nhìn thấy người mua nào cả: nó đọc dữ liệu sản phẩm.

chunks.h: Cần biết gì trước khi tin vào các con số?

chunks.t:
Mọi thay đổi trên các trang này, mới nhất trước, đọc trực tiếp từ git khi dựng site chứ không viết tay.

Trang này ghi lại điều gì đã thay đổi trên site và vào lúc nào. Danh sách được đọc từ lịch sử của
chính kho mã khi site được dựng, nên nó không thể lệch khỏi những gì thực sự đã xảy ra và không ai
phải nhớ cập nhật nó.

Đây không phải nhật ký thay đổi của API. 
 Quy tắc tương thích của API, thế nào là thay đổi phá vỡ, và chúng tôi có trách nhiệm gì khi điều
 đó xảy ra, nằm ở Phiên bản. API được đánh phiên bản theo URL còn các
 hướng dẫn thì không , đó là lựa chọn có chủ đích và được giải thích ở trang đó. Trang này là
 lịch sử của chính bộ tài liệu.
Nội dung commit được giữ nguyên tiếng Anh, vì đó là ngôn ngữ của kho mã.

chunks.h: Xem lịch sử của từng trang
chunks.t:
Mỗi trang đều hiển thị ngày sửa đổi gần nhất ở cuối trang, kèm liên kết tới toàn bộ lịch sử commit
của riêng tệp đó. Đây là cách nhanh nhất để trả lời câu hỏi "tháng trước trang này có viết khác
không", vốn thường mới là câu hỏi thật sự.

Các trang là tệp MDX trong
 content/docs , nên lịch sử chính
là git thông thường: mọi lần sửa, ai sửa, và những gì khác đã thay đổi trong cùng một commit.

Kết nối tài liệu PULSE với Claude, Cursor hoặc bất kỳ MCP client nào, để tác tử tìm và đọc đúng trang thay vì đoán.

Mọi trang trên site này đều có thể truy cập bằng tác tử qua Model Context Protocol. Một trợ lý đã
kết nối sẽ tìm trong tài liệu và trích dẫn, thay vì nhớ nhầm một endpoint không tồn tại.

Công cụ Làm gì 
 --- --- 
 search docs Tìm toàn văn trên mọi trang. Trả về đúng mục khớp, URL và điểm số 
 get page Một trang dạng Markdown, theo đường dẫn, ví dụ /quickstart hay /api/v1/audit 
 list pages Mọi trang kèm tiêu đề, để định hướng trước khi tìm 

Cả ba đều nhận lang là en hoặc vi .

chunks.h: Vì sao tìm theo từ khoá chứ không phải theo ngữ nghĩa?
chunks.t:
Website nhúng câu hỏi của bạn bằng một mô hình mà nó đã tải sẵn. Bắt một tác tử tải mô hình chỉ để
đặt câu hỏi là đánh đổi không đáng, vì bản thân tác tử đã là một mô hình ngôn ngữ: nó đọc ba mục
ứng viên và tự quyết định tốt hơn nhiều so với một phép cosine.

Thêm nữa, một tác tử hỏi về /catalog/audit muốn đúng trang chứa chuỗi đó, và tìm theo từ khoá
chính xác ở điểm này trong khi embedding thì làm nhoè đi.

chunks.h: Muốn trỏ sang nơi khác thì sao?
chunks.t:
Đặt PULSE DOCS ORIGIN để đọc từ một origin khác, chủ yếu hữu ích khi bạn đang sửa chính tài liệu
này:

 bash
PULSE DOCS ORIGIN=http://localhost:3000 npx @thepulseapi/docs-mcp

Được, và không cần MCP.

 
 --- --- 
 /llms.txt Mọi trang, có tiêu đề và liên kết, trong một tệp 
 /llms-full.txt Toàn bộ tài liệu gộp thành một tài liệu Markdown 
 /llms.mdx/docs/<path /content.md Một trang bất kỳ dạng Markdown 
 /search-index.json Kho văn bản đã chia khối kèm vector 

Mỗi trang cũng có nút Sao chép Markdown , là cách nhanh nhất khi bạn chỉ muốn dán một trang vào
cuộc hội thoại.
